title: Nvidia takeover of chip designer Arm investigated
summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has launched an investigation into Nvidia's proposed $40bn takeover of British chip designer Arm Holdings. The CMA will examine the merger's potential impact on competition, particularly concerning Arm's intellectual property licensing services to Nvidia's rivals. summary: NIO and NVIDIA have announced a partnership to develop a new generation of automated driving electric vehicles, with NIO selecting NVIDIA DRIVE Orin™ system-on-a-chip (SoC) for its future EVs. The first model to feature the NVIDIA DRIVE Orin-powered supercomputer, dubbed Adam, will be the ET7 sedan, set to ship in China in 2022. This collaboration aims to accelerate autonomous driving development, with NIO’s in-house algorithms running on four NVIDIA Orin processors to achieve over 1,000 TOPS performance.

summary: NVIDIA is bringing its 2nd generation Ampere RTX architecture to laptops, launching over 70 new GeForce RTX gaming and creator laptops starting January 26th. summary: NVIDIA has launched over 70 new GeForce RTX 30 Series laptops powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, offering up to 2x efficiency and featuring third-generation Max-Q technology. summary: Intel Corp. has appointed VMware CEO Pat Gelsinger as its new Chief Executive, replacing Robert Swan. summary: Intel is reportedly planning to outsource the manufacturing of its 7nm GPUs to TSMC, due to internal struggles with 7nm chip development. While Intel has historically manufactured its own processors, this move signifies a shift towards outsourcing to keep pace with rivals like AMD and Nvidia, who already use TSMC for their 7nm products. summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), a major chip supplier, announced plans to significantly increase its capital expenditures to between $25 billion and $28 billion in 2021. title: Nvidia’s Quadratic Processor, the NV1
summary: This article details Nvidia's ambitious first product, the NV1, a multimedia accelerator launched in 1995. Despite a significant deal with Sega, the industry was not ready for its advanced design, leading to its commercial failure before Nvidia pivoted to polygon-based designs and later achieved success with the Riva 128.

This funding aims to accelerate R&D and commercialization of its self-driving technologies, with trials of its Mini Robobus expected this month.

title: Werner Invests in TuSimple to Spur Autonomous Trucking

This program allows customers to remotely test Supermicro's 2U HGX A100 4-GPU or 4U HGX A100 8-GPU systems, enabling them to qualify their advanced workloads on high-performance platforms. The initiative aims to accelerate time-to-market solutions for AI and HPC applications by providing access to cutting-edge NVIDIA HGX A100 technology.

title: Chinese hacking group ‘Chimera’ targets Taiwanese chip and airline companies
summary: A Chinese advanced threat protection group named "Chimera" is reportedly targeting Taiwanese semiconductor companies to steal intelligence such as IC chip documents, SDKs, IC designs, and source code. title: Gemini-1 Spreads Millions of Processors Into RAM
summary: GSI Technology introduces Gemini-1, a processor-in-memory chip that accelerates specific mathematical functions by up to 100x compared to traditional processors. Designed as an "associative processing unit" (APU), Gemini-1 integrates about 2 million simple processing elements directly within SRAM cells, making it highly specialized for parallel search and cryptography algorithms. While not a general-purpose CPU, it excels at tasks like Hamming distance and Tanimoto similarity calculations by eliminating the data transfer bottleneck between CPU and RAM.

title: Changing Of The Guard For HPC And Big Iron At HPE
summary: Pete Ungaro, the long-time head of Cray and then HPE's High Performance Computing & Mission Critical Solutions group, is stepping down, with Justin Hotard taking over. The V1 core is designed for high-performance computing and enterprise workloads, offering significantly better single-threaded integer performance than its predecessor, while the N2 core optimizes for performance per dollar and watt, targeting mainstream infrastructure servers. These new designs, based on the upcoming Armv9-A architecture, highlight Arm's continued push into the server market with tailored solutions.

title: Apple Finally Feels the Effects of the Global Chip Shortage
summary: Apple Inc. reported strong revenue and record sales in its latest quarter, but warned that the global chip shortage is beginning to impact its business. Executives stated that supply constraints would specifically affect iPad and Mac sales, potentially reducing third-quarter revenue by $3 billion to $4 billion. This marks the first significant impact of the chip shortage on Apple's previously resilient production.

The report also includes recent news headlines related to Aptorum Group's stock.

title: Apple’s new M1 chip creates a competitive advantage
summary: Apple has introduced new iMacs and iPad Pros featuring its M1 chip, allowing the company to control its entire technology stack and gain a competitive advantage. This strategy insulates Apple from the global chip shortage affecting other manufacturers reliant on third-party semiconductors. Experts like Richard Barnett highlight that Apple's approach contrasts sharply with the challenges faced by automotive, consumer electronics, and medical device industries.

The fund invests in constituents of the S&P 500 Shariah Index, excluding specific sub-industries like Aerospace & Defense and Financial Exchanges.

title: Intel to Spend USD $3.5 Billion to Upgrade New Mexico Factory; More Exciting Chips Soon?
summary: Intel plans to invest $3.5 billion to upgrade its New Mexico factory, aiming to boost domestic chip manufacturing and address the global semiconductor shortage. This move is also a strategic response to competitors like AMD, enabling potentially lower chip costs and increased availability of upcoming products such as the 12th Gen Alder Lake processors and a powerful gaming-grade Xe-HPG graphics card. Intel's investment signals a push towards innovation and expanded in-house production, including custom chips for third-party clients.

title: Intel’s $3.5B New Mexico Campus Upgrade To Boost Next-Gen Chips
summary: Intel is investing $3.5 billion to upgrade its New Mexico manufacturing site, enabling it to produce next-generation processors with Foveros 3D packaging technology. This investment is part of Intel's new IDM 2.0 strategy, which aims to enhance performance, create jobs, and regain leadership in the chip market. The Foveros technology will allow Intel to stack chip tiles vertically, offering greater flexibility and performance in a smaller footprint.

title: NVIDIA Merlin Latest Enhancements Streamlines Recommender Workflows with .5 Release | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: NVIDIA Merlin's .5 update introduces key enhancements to streamline recommender workflows for machine learning engineers. The update includes a configurable data generator for training, a multi-GPU dataloader, and initial support for session-based recommenders, which are gaining attention for their ability to increase prediction accuracy with dynamic user interests. These additions reinforce NVIDIA's commitment to democratizing and accelerating the development of effective recommender systems.

title: These Were Nvidia’s 5 Most Highly Compensated Executives Last Year
summary: Nvidia's top five executives received higher compensation in fiscal year 2021, largely due to increased stock awards and incentive pay tied to the company's strong performance in data center and gaming markets. CEO Jensen Huang was the most compensated, earning $19.3 million, with his and other executives' base salaries slightly increasing due to an extra week in the fiscal year. The article details the compensation breakdown for each of the five highest-paid executives, highlighting the significant growth in their total earnings compared to the previous year.

title: STMicroelectronics Tackles the EV Industry with GaN
summary: STMicroelectronics is focusing on gallium nitride (GaN) technology to enhance efficiency in electric vehicle applications, recognizing its superiority over silicon in high-power scenarios. The company has released a new family of GaN devices called STi2GaN, specifically designed for the automotive industry, which integrates power stages, drivers, and protection within GaN and SiP solutions. This move aligns with STMicroelectronics' earlier commitment to invest in wide-bandgap semiconductors for carbon neutrality goals.

title: Redwood City startup Mythic scores $70M to challenge Nvidia on AI chips
summary: Redwood City-based startup Mythic has successfully raised $70 million to further develop its AI chips, positioning itself to challenge market leader Nvidia. Mythic is part of a new wave of semiconductor companies aiming to create chips that outperform existing options for AI tasks. This funding round highlights increasing competition in the AI chip market.

title: Z by HP Powers Creative Collaboration Everywhere for Today’s Creators
summary: HP has introduced new ZBook Studio G8, ZBook Fury G8, and ZBook Power G8 mobile workstations, designed for professional creators and power users who need performance, reliability, and versatility in hybrid work environments. These new models offer powerful computing, collaborative tools like ZCentral Remote Boost, and enhanced security features, while also emphasizing sustainability through the use of recycled materials and energy-efficient manufacturing. The ZBook Studio G8 is highlighted as the most powerful mobile workstation of its size, the ZBook Fury G8 as the most expandable and customizable, and the ZBook Power G8 provides an affordable professional-grade option.

title: 10 Hot Data Center Technologies And Trends To Watch In 2021
summary: This article outlines ten significant data center technologies and trends for 2021, driven by the shift to remote work and a digital economy. Key themes include the rise of "as-a-service" models, massive investments by public cloud providers, increasing private equity in data centers, and heightened CPU innovation from Intel, AMD, and Nvidia. Additionally, the article highlights the growing importance of automation, sustainability, and edge computing in the data center industry.

title: NVIDIA Transforms Mainstream Laptops into Gaming Powerhouses with GeForce RTX 30 Series
summary: NVIDIA has launched a new line of GeForce RTX laptops, powered by the RTX 3050 Ti and 3050 Laptop GPUs, making real-time ray tracing and AI-based DLSS accessible to more gamers and creators starting at $799. These new laptops offer significant performance improvements, including being twice as fast as previous-generation systems, and introduce features like NVIDIA Reflex for low-latency esports and NVIDIA Broadcast for enhanced video conferencing and livestreaming. NVIDIA Studio laptops with RTX 30 Series GPUs also offer up to 2x faster performance for creative applications, empowering artists and video editors.

title: WeRide reaches series C at $3.3bn valuation
summary: WeRide, a China-based autonomous driving technology provider, has secured hundreds of millions of dollars in Series C funding, valuing the company at $3.3 billion. The capital will be used for research and development and commercialization activities. Investors in this round include IDG Capital, Homeric Capital, and Qiming Venture Partners, among others, following previous investments from companies like Yutong Group, SenseTime, and Nvidia.

title: Insiders reveal one big surprise about a rumored OLED Nintendo Switch Pro
summary: Rumors suggest an OLED Nintendo Switch Pro is in the works, with industry insiders weighing in on what an OLED screen and a more powerful CPU could mean for the new console. While some believe an OLED screen is a natural evolution and won't significantly impact price, others see it and a new CPU as major upgrades that will improve the handheld experience. The article highlights the speculative nature of these discussions, despite enthusiasm from fans.

title: S Korea unveils US$450bn chipmaking master plan
summary: South Korea has announced a monumental US$450 billion investment plan over the next decade to build the world’s largest chipmaking base, involving key players like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. This initiative, dubbed the "K-semiconductor belt," aims to boost semiconductor research and production, enhance the nation's advanced logic chip capabilities, and reduce reliance on external manufacturers, amidst a global race for chip dominance and ongoing supply shortages. The government will support the industry with significant tax breaks, infrastructure improvements, and training programs to compete with global leaders like TSMC.

title: Three Partners Named Top Rising Stars in M&A by The Deal
summary: Latham & Watkins partners Daniel Breslin, Saad Khanani, and Victoria VanStekelenburg have been recognized by The Deal as "Top Rising Stars: Class of 2021" in Mergers & Acquisitions. The article highlights their significant contributions to major M&A transactions, their individual deal-making philosophies, and their involvement in firm initiatives like training and diversity. Each partner shared insights into what drives their engagement and success in the M&A field.

title: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks Deliver Unprecedented Firewall Performance for 5G Cloud-Native Security with DPU Acceleration
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have partnered to create a high-performance cybersecurity solution for 5G cloud-native environments. Their joint offering combines the Palo Alto Next-Generation Firewall with the NVIDIA BlueField-2 Data Processing Unit (DPU) to achieve up to 100Gb/s throughput with 80% traffic offload. This collaboration results in a 6X throughput increase over traditional host-based firewall solutions, addressing the demanding security needs of modern 5G networks.

title: Nvidia sets 4-for-1 stock split, shares rise
summary: Nvidia Corp announced a four-for-one stock split to make its shares more affordable for investors, causing its stock to rise by 3%. This move follows similar splits by Apple and Tesla last year, with Nvidia's split requiring stockholder approval in June and effective mid-July.

title: NVIDIA Announces Four-for-One Stock Split, Pending Stockholder Approval at Annual Meeting Set for June 3
summary: NVIDIA announced a four-for-one stock split in the form of a stock dividend, pending stockholder approval at its annual meeting on June 3. The split aims to make stock ownership more accessible to investors and employees. If approved, stockholders of record on June 21, 2021, will receive three additional shares for every share held, with trading on a split-adjusted basis expected to begin on July 20.

title: Putting the Chip Shortage into the Context of Long-Term Trends
summary: The article analyzes the current global semiconductor shortage, attributing it to supply chain rigidities, high barriers to entry, and geopolitical tensions exacerbated by COVID-19. It highlights the long-term trends driving increased semiconductor demand, such as 5G, AI, and electric vehicles, and discusses how governments and companies are responding to secure future supply chains and potentially re-shore manufacturing.

title: May 2021 Product Update -What’s New
summary: The May 2021 Fusion 360 product update introduces several new features and improvements across usability, sketching & modeling, electronics, generative design, and manufacturing. Key enhancements include Augmented Reality support via USDz export, a revamped Learning Panel, and expanded learning content for Fusion 360 Extensions. The update also brings significant advancements in electronics design with Stop Mask support in 3D PCB, improved display dialogs, and new library parts, alongside new generative design capabilities like Transparent View and enhanced manufacturing support for Formlabs and SLM Solutions 3D printers, plus machine simulation as a preview feature.

title: Samsung, TSMC up ante in US foundry competition
summary: The world's two largest foundry chipmakers, TSMC and Samsung Electronics, are engaged in fierce competition to expand their presence in the US, driven by significant investment plans. Samsung announced a $17 billion investment for a US factory, following TSMC's $12 billion Arizona plant. This rivalry, coupled with Intel's entry into the foundry business, intensifies the competition in the advanced chip manufacturing market, with both companies risking substantial losses if they fail to secure enough clients for their costly new facilities.

title: SOXX Versus SOXL Semiconductor ETF Forecast: Which Is a Better Buy?
summary: This article compares two semiconductor ETFs, SOXX and SOXL, to determine which might be a better investment. SOXL is a leveraged ETF offering 3x daily returns, leading to higher performance during bull markets but also higher risk. SOXX is a plain ETF for risk-averse, long-term investors, with both ETFs holding similar top companies and having a positive medium-term outlook despite the cyclical nature of the industry.

title: Nvidia sold $155 million in crypto mining chips last quarter, but PC gaming remains its biggest market
summary: Nvidia reported $155 million in revenue from its new cryptocurrency mining processors (CMPs) in the last quarter, with projected sales of $400 million for the current quarter. Despite these figures, CEO Jensen Huang emphasizes that PC gaming remains the company's primary and most important market, generating $2.76 billion in revenue. The introduction of CMP chips is intended to protect the supply of graphics cards for gamers by diverting crypto miners from purchasing gaming-specific GPUs.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2022
summary: NVIDIA reported record revenue of $5.66 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2022, an 84% increase year-over-year, driven by strong growth in its Gaming and Data Center platforms. The company also announced a four-for-one stock split and provided an optimistic outlook for the second quarter, projecting revenue of $6.30 billion. Key highlights include advancements in Gaming with new RTX GPUs and DLSS adoption, and significant innovations in Data Center and Automotive sectors.

title: Stock of the week - NVIDIA (27.05.2021)
summary: NVIDIA (NVDA.US) reported record first-quarter fiscal 2022 results, exceeding revenue and EPS expectations, driven by strong performance in Gaming, Data Center, and Professional Visualization platforms. The company also announced an upbeat Q2 forecast and a 4-for-1 stock split, which is seen as a bullish signal for investors. The growth is significantly boosted by the gaming sector during the pandemic and the increasing demand for its graphics cards by cryptocurrency miners.

title: Vision Fund loss slashes Masayoshi Son’s 2020 salary by 52%
summary: SoftBank Group founder and CEO Masayoshi Son's salary was more than halved in 2020 to 100 million yen ($0.9 million), a 52% decrease from 2019, largely attributed to the Vision Fund's substantial losses in the 2019 financial year. However, with SoftBank posting a record-breaking net profit of 4.99 trillion yen in FY 2020, Son's salary is anticipated to rebound significantly in the current year. The article also notes recent investments by SoftBank's Vision Fund in companies like Yanolja and Balance Hero.

title: How Nvidia plans to own the data center with AI
summary: Nvidia aims to revolutionize enterprise computing by making data centers run 10 times faster at one-tenth the cost, leveraging its strong position in AI architectures. The company plans to disrupt Intel's x86 dominance through Arm-based architectures, integrated chip designs, and a compelling software consumption model. The article highlights Nvidia's strategic moves, financial standing, and the potential impact of its proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. on the data center market.

title: Rain pelts down in Taiwan to provide drought relief
summary: Taiwan is experiencing significant rainfall with "extremely heavy rain" advisories issued for central counties and "heavy rain" advisories for other regions. This rain provides some relief for the country's severe drought, with chip manufacturers like TSMC and UMC anticipating water restrictions to potentially be mitigated. Meteorologists predict continued strong fronts and thunderstorms through early next week before rainfall intensity may decrease.

title: NVIDIA AI Enterprise Software Drives New Wave of Certified Systems from World’s Leading Manufacturers
summary: NVIDIA announced a significant expansion of its NVIDIA-Certified Systems program, featuring dozens of new servers from leading manufacturers that are certified to run NVIDIA AI Enterprise software. These systems, including high-volume x86 servers, are designed to bring the power of AI to various industries by supporting demanding workloads in traditional data centers and hybrid clouds. The expansion also includes new servers equipped with BlueField-2 DPUs for enhanced security and upcoming Arm CPU servers for high-performance AI computing.

title: NVIDIA Base Command Platform Provides Enterprises with Fast Path to Scale Production AI
summary: NVIDIA announced the Base Command Platform, a cloud-hosted development hub designed to help enterprises streamline AI projects from prototype to production. This platform, available through a monthly subscription with NetApp, offers access to NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD AI supercomputers and NetApp data management. Google Cloud plans to integrate the platform into its marketplace, promoting a hybrid AI experience.

title: NVIDIA Partners Unveil New Servers Featuring NVIDIA BlueField DPUs
summary: Several top server manufacturers, including ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, QCT, and Supermicro, announced new systems at COMPUTEX 2021 featuring NVIDIA BlueField-2 Data Processing Units (DPUs). These DPUs enhance server performance, security, and manageability by offloading networking, storage, and cybersecurity tasks from the CPU, making more resources available for applications. The servers are designed for various enterprise applications and can be easily programmed using the NVIDIA DOCA SDK, with DPU-accelerated servers expected to be available later this year.

title: It’s Time for Ti: NVIDIA Introduces Gaming Flagship — the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti
summary: NVIDIA has announced two new additions to its GeForce RTX family: the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti and GeForce RTX 3070 Ti. The RTX 3080 Ti, launching June 3rd at $1,199, is touted as the new flagship gaming GPU, offering 1.5x faster performance than previous generations and catering to demanding modern games and creative applications. The RTX 3070 Ti, available next week starting at $599, also delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessors.

title: AMD shows how FidelityFX Super Resolution beats out NVIDIA's DLSS
summary: AMD announced FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) at Computex 2021, an image upscaling technology designed to boost frame rates and resolution. FSR directly competes with NVIDIA's DLSS but offers broader compatibility, supporting a wide range of AMD GPUs and even some NVIDIA GeForce cards. The technology, which provides up to a 2.5 times increase in performance mode, is expected to launch on June 22, 2021.

title: NVIDIA Announces Upcoming Events for Financial Community
summary: NVIDIA announced its participation in several upcoming financial community events in June 2021, including the Evercore ISI Inaugural TMT Conference, BofA 2021 Global Technology Conference, and Nasdaq 44th Investor Conference. Interested parties can access live audio webcasts of these presentations and replays on NVIDIA's investor relations website. The company also reiterated its role in pioneering accelerated computing and AI, highlighting its impact on various industries.

title: TSMC Throws The Ball In Intel’s Court By Showcasing Customized Chipmaking Technologies
summary: TSMC announced new customized semiconductor nodes, N5A for automotive and N6RF for communications, at its online technology symposium. This move aims to solidify TSMC's position as a contract chip manufacturer by offering specialized processes, directly challenging Intel's plans to enter the contract manufacturing space. TSMC emphasized its commitment to not competing with its customers, differentiating itself from other potential foundries.

title: How to View Your Fusion 360 Designs in AR with USDz File Format
summary: Fusion 360 has introduced support for the USDz file format, enabling users to view their 3D designs in augmented reality (AR) directly from iOS mobile devices. This feature allows designers to preview designs in real-life environments, assess scale and aesthetics, and communicate concepts more effectively to clients and stakeholders. The article explains what USDz is, how to export files from Fusion 360, and highlights the benefits of using AR for design visualization.

title: Here to stay: Implications and opportunities from Taiwan’s semiconductor edge
summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry dominance stems from decades of government policy and private sector innovation, creating a thriving ecosystem. This leadership is sustained by aggressive R&D investments and high barriers to entry, making it difficult for new competitors to catch up. Structural demand drivers like 5G, AI, and EVs are expected to fuel continued growth in semiconductor sales, presenting attractive opportunities for active investors within Taiwan's broader semiconductor ecosystem.

title: People camped out at Bakersfield Best Buy for upcoming graphics card
summary: Nearly one hundred people camped out at the Bakersfield Best Buy on Rosedale Highway for NVIDIA’s latest graphics card, the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Founders Edition. The card was set to be released on Thursday at select Best Buy stores nationwide, with customers lining up due to global chip shortages and high demand. Employees planned to hand out tickets at 7:30 a.m., guaranteeing purchase at 9 a.m. for those who received one.

title: Super Micro Computer To Double Their Manufacturing Capacity To Meet Worldwide Server And Storage Demands
summary: Super Micro Computer, Inc. is doubling its manufacturing capacity at its US and Taiwan campuses to meet the growing global demand for servers and storage driven by Cloud, AI, and 5G/Edge technologies. This expansion aims to increase production to over two million servers per year by mid-2021 and enable the company to ship fully tested racks directly to customers. Supermicro will offer a range of application-optimized systems, including those supporting the latest Intel and AMD processors, NVIDIA GPUs, and liquid cooling options, to accommodate various workloads.

title: AMD extends FidelityFX Super Resolution to RX 470 and RX 480
summary: AMD is extending its FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) technology to older graphics cards, specifically the Radeon RX 470 and RX 480 GPUs, dating back to 2016. This digital upscaling technology is designed to improve game performance and visuals without requiring significant processing power, and it will also work with a wide range of other AMD and some NVIDIA GeForce cards. FSR is expected to launch on June 22, 2021, offering performance boosts for both high-end and older hardware.

title: Marvell Extends PAM4 DSP Cloud Data Center Leadership with Industry's First Integrated Solution
summary: Marvell has announced its Atlas 50Gbps PAM4 DSP chipset solution, which integrates transimpedance amplifiers and laser drivers into a single mainstream CMOS technology solution. This advancement significantly reduces power consumption by 25% and simplifies the supply chain for high-performance cloud data centers, computing, and AI applications. The Atlas DSP platform is designed for high-volume markets, offering cost-effective, highly integrated, and reliable technology essential for massive data center growth.

title: Tilling AI: Startup Digs into Autonomous Electric Tractors for Organics
summary: Ztractor, founded by Bakur Kvezereli, is an autonomous electric tractor startup utilizing NVIDIA's Jetson edge AI platform to address labor shortages, pesticide issues, and energy costs in organic farming. The company offers tractors equipped with numerous sensors and cameras that collect data to improve crop conditions, increase yields, and enhance efficiency, positioning the agricultural machine industry for an "electric revolution" similar to the automotive sector. Ztractor's technology, which enables tasks like precision weeding and soil preparation, aims to make organic farming more competitive and sustainable.

title: New Cadence Allegro X Design Platform Revolutionizes System Design
summary: Cadence Design Systems introduces the Allegro X Design Platform, an integrated engineering solution for system design that unifies schematic, layout, analysis, collaboration, and data management. This new platform, built on Allegro and OrCAD technology, aims to significantly streamline the design process for engineers, offering up to 4X productivity improvements through enhanced integration, cloud capabilities, and ML-driven advancements. It supports complex multi-domain designs (EM, thermal, SI/PI) and leverages GPU technology for accelerated performance.

title: Opinion: AMD’s stock has been left behind, but not for long — here’s why
summary: The article argues that Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock is a good buy despite its significant past gains, as it hasn't fully rebounded from a recent dip unlike other semiconductor stocks like Nvidia. The author attributes this potential for future growth to AMD's new cutting-edge products and a key acquisition.

title: NVIDIA to Acquire DeepMap, Enhancing Mapping Solutions for the AV Industry
summary: NVIDIA has acquired DeepMap, a startup focused on creating high-definition maps for autonomous vehicles, to enhance its mapping products and accelerate full self-driving expertise. DeepMap's technology provides centimeter-level precision mapping and continuous updates, crucial for autonomous vehicles to navigate safely and accurately. This acquisition strengthens NVIDIA's DRIVE platform by improving localization capabilities for AVs.

title: Report: Intel has offered $2B+ to acquire chip startup SiFive
summary: Intel Corp. has reportedly offered over $2 billion to acquire SiFive Inc., a chip startup specializing in processor technology based on the open-source RISC-V instruction set architecture. This potential acquisition would be one of Intel's largest recent deals, following its 2019 purchase of Habana Labs. The move could position Intel to address future demand for open-source chip designs, especially given concerns surrounding Nvidia's acquisition of Arm.

Each ETF is designed to support different investment goals but comes with specific risks that investors should carefully assess against their individual objectives. title: Rumor: Intel May Buy RISC-V CPU Designer SiFive to Fend off ARM
summary: A rumor suggests Intel is considering purchasing RISC-V CPU design company SiFive for $2.1 billion. This acquisition could provide Intel with a significant stake in the expanding RISC-V market, complementing its foundry efforts and potentially positioning RISC-V alongside x86 in specific market segments. The move is also seen as a strategic response to Nvidia's potential acquisition of ARM, allowing Intel to hedge its bets in the evolving CPU landscape, though SiFive's open-source nature means other companies could still develop RISC-V CPUs.

title: Nvidia acquires DeepMap as it builds out its end-to-end autonomous driving stack
summary: Nvidia has announced its acquisition of DeepMap Inc., a startup specializing in mapping technology for autonomous vehicles. This acquisition aims to enhance Nvidia's comprehensive suite of solutions for the autonomous driving sector, which already includes chips, software tools, and simulation platforms. The integration of DeepMap's technology will allow Nvidia to strengthen its competitive position against rivals like Intel's Mobileye unit by improving its mapping capabilities for self-driving cars.

summary: The Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXQ) has launched, tracking the PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index (SOX), which comprises 30 components integral to disruptive technologies like NVIDIA and Qualcomm. Despite a global semiconductor shortage, the SOX index has outperformed the Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500 this year, showcasing strong growth in revenue and net income for its large-cap constituents. This new ETF offers investors exposure to the long-term growth potential of the semiconductor industry, driven by demand from everyday consumer items and advanced technologies like AI and cloud computing.

title: Trash to Cash: Recyclers Tap Startup with World’s Largest Recycling Network to Freshen Up Business Prospects
summary: AMP Robotics, founded by Matanya Horowitz, uses AI powered by NVIDIA GPUs to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recycling. The startup addresses the challenge of contaminated recyclables and the high costs associated with manual sorting by deploying robotic arms that utilize computer vision to identify and sort various materials with high precision. This technology helps recyclers increase purity, reduce operational costs, and generate more revenue from sorted materials.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is the World’s Most Important Chip Maker. How to Play the Stock.
summary: The article highlights Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) as the world's most critical chipmaker, responsible for approximately 60% of outsourced chip manufacturing and 90% of the industry's profits. It notes that the ongoing semiconductor shortage has emphasized the importance of chips across various sectors, from simple components to high-end processors. The article then addresses how investors can approach this significant stock.

summary: This article provides details on the Dimensional U.S. Core Equity 2 ETF (NYSEARCA:DFAC), an exchange-traded fund that invests in U.S. equities with a tilt towards small-cap companies. title: Bernstein recommends Sea, says Singapore-based internet company is a 'super app in the making'
summary: Bernstein recommends Sea Ltd., calling the Singapore-based internet company a "super app in the making" and initiating coverage with an outperform rating and a $350 price target. The investment firm believes Sea's strong execution track record ensures its dominance in various verticals, particularly highlighting the potential of its e-commerce arm, Shopee, to reach breakeven by 2025. Key drivers for the stock are expected to be Shopee's expansion in Latin America and grocery in Southeast Asia, leading to increased profitability.

title: Nvidia Share Price: Why Stock Split Means ‘Nothing’ to CNBC's Jim Cramer
summary: Nvidia's stock split, recently approved by shareholders, is set to make shares more accessible by reducing the price per share while increasing the number of shares held by investors. Despite a rally following the announcement, CNBC's Jim Cramer believes the split "does nothing" to increase Nvidia's appeal, arguing that investors should focus on company fundamentals rather than stock gimmicks. Analysts currently maintain a "buy" rating on Nvidia, with an average price target that suggests a slight downside from its recent trading price, though one analyst sees significant upside potential in its gaming business.

title: This is Grand Theft Auto as made by AI
summary: AI researchers have utilized Nvidia's GameGAN neural network to create "GAN Theft Auto," an entirely AI-generated version of Grand Theft Auto V. The playable demo showcases an AI-generated highway scene that, despite being pixelated, demonstrates impressive details like shadows and reflections, all without human-coded graphics. This project offers a glimpse into a future where entire games, or portions thereof, could be concocted by AI.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Acquires AI Company Determined AI to Focus on Accelerating Machine Learning
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has acquired AI startup Determined AI to accelerate machine learning models. Determined AI, founded by UC Berkeley researchers, specializes in open-source machine learning platforms that significantly reduce computation time for AI model training. This acquisition aims to combine HPE's high-performance computing with Determined AI's technology to simplify AI development and shorten time to market.

title: Longtime Intel exec Navin Shenoy leaves as chipmaker restructures data center business
summary: Longtime Intel executive Navin Shenoy is departing the company as CEO Pat Gelsinger implements a major restructuring of its critical data center business, creating two new units. The Data Platform Group is being split into a Datacenter and AI group led by Sandra Rivera, and a Network and Edge Group led by Nick McKeown. Additionally, Intel is forming a Software and Advanced Technology Group and an Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics Group, led by Greg Lavender and Raja Koduri respectively, to better compete with rivals like Nvidia, Arm Ltd., Qualcomm Corp., and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

title: Intel Restructuring: Navin Shenoy Out; New Software, GPU Units
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has announced a major restructuring of the company, leading to the departure of top data center executive Navin Shenoy. The Data Platform Group is being split into two new business units, and two new divisions, the Software and Advanced Technology Group and the Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics Group, are being formed. These changes aim to accelerate Intel's pace in regaining technology leadership, with new leaders appointed to head the reorganized groups.

title: Unity acquires Pixyz Software
summary: Unity Technologies has acquired France-based Pixyz Software, a specialist in 3D data optimization, for an undisclosed sum. Pixyz's technology, which helps developers import and edit 3D models in real-time, will be integrated into Unity's Create segment, but will continue to charge a separate subscription. This acquisition is part of Unity's strategy to expand its business through targeted takeovers, enhancing its offerings for both gaming and industrial customers.

title: GlobalFoundries to open new fab in Singapore
summary: GlobalFoundries is investing $4 billion to build a new semiconductor fabrication plant in Singapore, aiming to expand its manufacturing capacity amidst a global chip shortage. The facility, expected to roll out its first production wafers in Q1 2023, will create 1,000 high-value jobs and strengthen Singapore's position in advanced manufacturing. This expansion is designed to meet surging demand driven by 5G, IoT, and cloud computing.

title: 3D interactive tour of ONTAP AI
summary: NetApp offers a 3D interactive tour of its ONTAP AI proven architecture, which combines NVIDIA DGX systems with NetApp cloud-connected all-flash storage to accelerate AI workloads. The tour allows users to explore various configurations, including NVIDIA DGX A100 servers and NetApp AFF A400 and A800 storage systems, with detailed views of individual components. This solution is designed to streamline data flow and speed up analytics, training, and inference across a data fabric from edge to core to cloud.

title: NVIDIA Fleet Command Scales Edge AI Services for Enterprises
summary: NVIDIA has launched its Fleet Command managed edge AI services platform, designed to simplify the deployment and management of AI applications across thousands of locations for enterprises. This SaaS platform helps businesses securely roll out and manage AI applications on NVIDIA-Certified Systems, reducing IT burden and accelerating the adoption of AI in various industries. Early adopters include leading companies in retail, healthcare, and logistics, using Fleet Command to improve operational efficiency and address complex challenges in edge AI deployment.

title: NVIDIA Announces Instant AI Infrastructure for Enterprises
summary: NVIDIA has launched AI LaunchPad, a program that provides enterprises with immediate access to NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and software to streamline the entire AI lifecycle. Digital infrastructure leader Equinix is the first partner, offering NVIDIA-powered hybrid-cloud solutions globally that deploy in minutes. This initiative aims to simplify AI deployment for businesses by providing a comprehensive, ready-to-use hybrid-cloud platform.

title: Tesla Unveils Top AV Training Supercomputer Powered by NVIDIA A100 GPUs
summary: Tesla has unveiled its in-house supercomputer, powered by 5,760 NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, to train deep neural networks for its Autopilot and self-driving capabilities. This system achieves an industry-leading 1.8 exaflops of performance, making it one of the top five supercomputers globally. The supercomputer is crucial for processing massive datasets from Tesla's fleet of over a million vehicles, allowing for continuous iteration and refinement of their autonomous driving AI.

title: HPE should add bank card swipe to on-prem cloud for growth, says analyst
summary: A disruptive technology analyst suggests that HPE's on-premises cloud solutions, like GreenLake, should incorporate credit card payment options to offer developers greater flexibility and agility, mimicking public cloud advantages. This would enable easy scaling of workloads and position HPE to capitalize on the shift of data and compute to the edge. The article emphasizes the importance of edge computing, detailing the challenges and opportunities for on-prem vendors, and also touches on the future of the semiconductor industry with increased competition.

title: Nvidia’s Vid2Vid Cameo AI brings 2D photos to life in video calls
summary: Nvidia has introduced Vid2Vid Cameo, a deep learning model that enables users to display a chosen 2D image or avatar during video calls, animated by their real-time movements and facial expressions. This AI technology, soon available in the Nvidia Maxine SDK, aims to enhance professionalism, reduce bandwidth consumption, and minimize video call jitter and lag. It works by mapping 20 key facial points from a live video feed to a reference image, then synthesizing a new video stream on the receiver's end, requiring significantly less bandwidth than traditional video.

title: Volvo plans to add lidar as standard equipment in electric XC90 SUV next year
summary: Volvo Cars announced plans to make lidar sensors standard equipment in its electric XC90 SUV starting next year, a strategic move to enhance safety and autonomous driving. This decision positions Volvo differently from rivals like Tesla, which rely solely on cameras. Luminar Technologies Inc. will supply the Iris lidar and Sentinel software for this integration.

title: ACGR ETF Profile: Dividends, Returns (BOATS:ACGR)
summary: The ACGR ETF (American Century Large Cap Growth ETF) is an actively managed fund that invests in large-cap stocks, utilizing a multi-factor model combining financial and ESG scores. The ETF holds a diversified portfolio primarily in Electronic Technology and Technology Services, with significant exposure to North America. It pays quarterly dividends and has an expense ratio of 0.39%.

title: Nvidia’s takeover of Arm gets support from Broadcom and other chip heavyweights
summary: Broadcom, MediaTek, and Marvell have publicly expressed their support for Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, despite scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from rivals like Qualcomm, Google, and Microsoft. These chip heavyweights cite assurances from Nvidia regarding increased investment in Arm's technology and continued fair access for the industry. The support comes as Nvidia and Arm CEOs argue the deal is necessary to meet growing demand and accelerate technological roadmaps in the semiconductor industry amidst a global chip shortage.

title: Boost performance with NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage
summary: This article discusses how NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage (MIO GDS) can significantly boost performance for AI and data-intensive workloads by enabling direct data transfers between GPU memory and storage, bypassing the CPU. It highlights NetApp's AI solutions for NVIDIA DGX A100 systems, explaining how NetApp AFF and EF-Series arrays with BeeGFS integrate to leverage GDS for improved bandwidth and lower latency. The author, Mike McNamara, emphasizes the benefits for various industries and NetApp's role as a key NVIDIA partner in delivering these high-performance storage solutions.

title: NVIDIA and Global Partners Launch New HGX A100 Systems to Accelerate Industrial AI and HPC
summary: NVIDIA has enhanced its HGX AI supercomputing platform with new technologies designed to accelerate industrial AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC). The updates include the NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe GPU, NVIDIA NDR 400G InfiniBand networking, and NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage software, aiming to deliver extreme performance for innovation. Partners like Atos, Dell Technologies, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise are integrating these advancements into their next-generation systems, leveraging the platform to address complex challenges in various industries.

title: Nvidia integrates Arm processors with its 5G edge infrastructure platform
summary: Nvidia has announced the integration of Arm processors into its Nvidia Aerial A100 AI-on-5G platform, expanding its capabilities for 5G applications at the network edge. This move provides more choice for users, as the platform previously supported only x86-based CPUs from Intel. Additionally, Nvidia is partnering with Google LLC to establish an AI-on-5G Innovation Lab, aiming to accelerate the adoption and development of solutions on this combined AI and 5G platform.

title: Graphcore brings new competition to Nvidia in latest MLPerf AI benchmarks
summary: Graphcore, a UK-based startup, has demonstrated competitive performance against industry giants Nvidia and Google in the latest MLPerf AI benchmarks. While not securing the top spot in any test, Graphcore's results are significant when considering the fewer chips used and its commercial availability, positioning it as a viable alternative in the AI training market. Despite Nvidia's claims of "cherry-picking" comparisons and maintaining a strong overall lead, Graphcore emphasizes the economic advantage and scalability of its IPU systems.

title: Invesco S&P 500 QVM Multi-factor ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:QVML)
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 QVM Multi-factor ETF (QVML) is an exchange-traded fund that tracks a market-cap-weighted index of the top 90% of S&P 500 stocks based on quality, value, and momentum factors. Launched on June 30, 2021, and managed by Invesco, QVML currently has $1.54 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.11%. Its stock has increased by 14.1% year-to-date, trading at $45.84, and its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Alphabet.

title: Texas Instruments to buy semiconductor factory in $900 million deal
summary: Texas Instruments announced it will acquire Micron Technology Inc.'s semiconductor factory in Lehi, Utah, for $900 million in cash. This acquisition will be TI's fourth 300-millimeter wafer facility, strengthening its manufacturing capabilities and supply chain control amid a global chip shortage. The company expects the plant to begin generating revenue in the first quarter of 2023, following an investment of approximately $75 million per quarter in 2022.

title: D-MARKET Electronic Services & Trading (HEPS) Stock Price, News & Analysis $HEPS
summary: This article provides an analysis of D-MARKET Electronic Services & Trading (HEPS) stock, including its current price, analyst ratings, and financial performance. It highlights the company's e-commerce operations in Turkey, its various services like Hepsiburada Market and Hepsipay, and key financial metrics. The consensus analyst rating is "Reduce" with a price target of $3.07, and the company does not currently pay a dividend.

title: Advisor Ross Gerber Launches Active 'Roaring '20s' ETF
summary: Advisor Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, has launched an actively managed ETF called the AdvisorShares Gerber Kawasaki ETF (GK). This new ETF will focus on nine investment themes Gerber believes will thrive in the post-COVID economy, offering investors access to his stock-picking expertise in a tax-efficient structure. Gerber emphasizes that the ETF is designed as a core growth fund for long-term investors, not a "get-rich-quick" scheme, and aims to provide a smoother ride than more volatile single-theme funds.

title: Focus: Qualcomm's new CEO eyes dominance in the laptop markets
summary: Qualcomm's new CEO, Cristiano Amon, plans to challenge Apple's dominance in the laptop market by developing energy-efficient chips with the help of former Apple chip architects. The company is also focusing on revenue growth from China for its smartphone chip business despite political tensions and aims to leverage its Nuvia acquisition to push 5G connectivity into laptops, providing custom-designed chips to compete with Apple. Amon also faces the challenge of potentially losing Apple as a modem chip customer and improving Qualcomm's brand recognition among consumers.

title: AvePoint (AVPT) Stock Price, News & Analysis
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of AvePoint (AVPT) stock, including its current price, analyst ratings, financial health, earnings, and news sentiment. AvePoint specializes in data management and compliance solutions for Microsoft 365, with analysts giving it a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating and projecting significant upside potential. The company's stock has faced a recent downturn, but future earnings growth is expected.

title: NVIDIA Launches UK’s Most Powerful Supercomputer, for Research in AI and Healthcare
summary: NVIDIA has launched Cambridge-1, the UK's most powerful supercomputer, to accelerate AI and simulation research in digital biology and healthcare. This $100 million investment will support projects with key partners like AstraZeneca and GSK to advance drug discovery, understand brain diseases, and improve genomic accuracy. The supercomputer is a NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD cluster, powered by 100% renewable energy, and aims to generate £600 million in economic value over the next decade.

title: NVIDIA debuts supercomputer for healthcare and AI research
summary: NVIDIA has launched the Cambridge-1, acclaimed as the UK's most powerful supercomputer, with a $100 million investment aimed at healthcare applications. The supercomputer will utilize AI to advance drug development, explore dementia causes, and identify genomic disease risk factors. AstraZeneca and GSK are among the early users, leveraging its capabilities for chemical structure modeling, digital pathology, and genetic validation of drug targets.

title: Intel Corporation names Shlomit Weiss as co-General Manager of its Design Engineering Group
summary: Shlomit Weiss is returning to Intel as Senior Vice President and co-General Manager of its Design Engineering Group, where she will oversee chip development for client computers. Weiss, who previously spent 28 years at Intel and most recently served as Senior VP for Silicon Engineering at Nvidia, will work from Israel alongside Sunil Shenoy. She brings extensive experience, having been recognized for developing Intel's Dual-Core processor architecture and leading the Sky Lake processor development.

title: Nvidia launches $100M Cambridge-1 supercomputer to support healthcare research
summary: Nvidia has launched Cambridge-1, a $100 million supercomputer in the U.K. dedicated to life sciences research. It is the fastest supercomputer in the U.K., offering eight petaflops with Linpack and 400 petaflops for AI workloads, powered entirely by renewable energy. The system will support various research projects with partners like AstraZeneca, GSK, King's College London, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, and Oxford Nanopore Technologies, focusing on drug discovery, disease understanding, and algorithm improvement.

title: Qualcomm and InterDigital among founders of new US 6G initiative
summary: A new 6G initiative named 6G@UT has been launched in the US, based at the University of Texas in Austin, with key founders including Qualcomm, InterDigital, AT&T, Nvidia, and Samsung. This initiative aims to advance 6G research with a strong focus on embedding machine learning and sensing technologies, anticipating a future where AI/ML will fundamentally transform wireless communications. The founding members emphasize the importance of collaborative research to develop intelligent networks capable of providing advanced services and supporting futuristic applications like holographic calls and immersive AR/VR.

title: JPMorgan U.S. Research Enhanced Large Cap ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:JUSA)
summary: The JPMorgan U.S. Research Enhanced Large Cap ETF (JUSA) is an actively managed ETF focusing on large-cap US equities, launched on July 7, 2021, and managed by JPMorgan Chase. The ETF has seen a 7.6% increase in its stock price since the beginning of the year and currently has $204.68 million in assets under management. Its top holdings include major technology companies like NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon.com.

title: Ash Bhalgat Author Page
summary: This page introduces Ash Bhalgat, Senior Director of AI Networking and Security Solutions at NVIDIA, detailing his 25 years of high-tech experience at companies like Cisco and Polycom. It highlights his expertise in various technologies, including data centers, AI, and cybersecurity. The page also features articles he's associated with, such as collaborations between NVIDIA and F5, and NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks, to enhance AI efficiency and cyber defenses.

title: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks Boost Cyber Defenses with DPU Acceleration
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have partnered to enhance cybersecurity by accelerating Palo Alto Networks' virtual next-generation firewall (NGFW) with NVIDIA's BlueField data processing unit (DPU). This collaboration significantly boosts firewall performance by offloading packet filtering and forwarding, achieving a 5x performance increase and enabling intelligent traffic offload. The new solution allows for comprehensive security coverage across all servers without compromising network speed, addressing the rising costs and sophistication of cybercrime.

title: AutoX Unveils Full Self-Driving System Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: AutoX has launched its "Gen5" self-driving system, designed specifically for robotaxis and powered by NVIDIA DRIVE automotive-grade GPUs, achieving up to 2,200 TOPS of AI compute performance. This system enables full self-driving mobility services without a safety driver, as demonstrated in Shenzhen, China, and is central to AutoX's plans for a global robotaxi rollout. The Gen5 system utilizes 28 cameras, six lidar sensors, and 4D radar to navigate complex urban environments, with NVIDIA Ampere architecture GPUs providing the necessary processing power for advanced AI.

title: Is Nvidia Stock A Buy Now Before Its Stock Split? (NASDAQ:NVDA)
summary: NVIDIA has announced a stock split effective July 20, which historically can lead to short-term price movements. While growth and valuation are long-term drivers, NVIDIA is well-positioned for future growth but its shares are currently historically expensive. The article explores whether NVIDIA is a buy before its upcoming stock split, considering both its growth prospects and current valuation.

title: Nvidia reveals how its BlueField DPUs boost Palo Alto Networks' virtual firewall performance
summary: Palo Alto Networks and Nvidia detailed their collaboration on a massively accelerated virtual next-generation firewall (NGFW) that uses Nvidia's BlueField-2 Data Processing Units (DPUs) to offload network traffic inspection from server CPUs, significantly boosting performance. The VM-Series NGFW can achieve 100 gigabytes per second throughput, a five-times improvement over CPU-only firewalls, by utilizing the DPUs for intelligent traffic filtering and offloading uninspectable or unnecessary traffic. This approach allows server CPUs to focus on compute tasks and optimizes firewall efficiency without compromising security.

title: XYLG Stock Price | Global X S&P 500 Covered Call & Growth ETF
summary: This page provides detailed information about the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call & Growth ETF (XYLG), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NYSE), and key statistics like dividend yield, expense ratio, and market cap. It also offers insights into its performance, top holdings, and technical analysis, making it a comprehensive resource for potential investors.

title: What’s fuelling growth in the Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF?
summary: The Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV) has shown significant growth, fueled by increasing demand for electric and autonomous vehicles and government initiatives supporting green energy. Top holdings include Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, and Toyota, reflecting investment in both hardware and software for this disruptive technology. Despite potential challenges like volatility and supply chain issues, analysts believe the ETF offers diversified exposure to the booming EV sector.

title: PTC Collaborates with NVIDIA and NetApp to Launch AI Integration Hub
summary: PTC System (S) Pte Ltd has launched an AI Integration Hub in collaboration with NVIDIA and NetApp to help enterprises leverage AI and data science. The hub is built on NetApp ONTAP AI, combining NVIDIA DGX systems and NetApp All Flash FAS, and aims to accelerate the deployment of AI applications by offering free testing services. This initiative, supported by key executives from PTC, NetApp, and NVIDIA, seeks to boost AI adoption across the Asia-Pacific region, including Singapore, by providing high-performance computing infrastructure and simplified AI deployment paths.

title: Intel exploring deal to buy US chipmaker GlobalFoundries for $30B
summary: Intel Corp. is reportedly in talks to acquire chipmaker GlobalFoundries Inc. for up to $30 billion, which would be Intel's largest acquisition to date. The potential deal aligns with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger's strategy to bolster the company's chip production capabilities and compete with industry leaders like TSMC. Analysts note the acquisition could offer immediate benefits to Intel by providing access to more fabs, while GlobalFoundries' owners would secure a significant payday without the uncertainty of an IPO.

title: Intel is in talks to buy GlobalFoundries for about $30 billion
summary: Intel is reportedly in discussions to acquire GlobalFoundries for approximately $30 billion, a move that would significantly boost Intel's strategy to become a major contract chip manufacturer. This potential acquisition aligns with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger's push to expand chip-making capabilities for other companies, a market currently dominated by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The deal, if it materializes, would be Intel's largest acquisition ever, although GlobalFoundries is also considering an initial public offering.

title: AEye’s LiDAR to be Available on The NVIDIA DRIVE Autonomous Vehicle Platform
summary: AEye, Inc. announced its adaptive, intelligent LiDAR solutions will be available on the NVIDIA DRIVE autonomous vehicle platform. This collaboration will provide ADAS and AV developers with advanced tools to enhance data quality for Level 2+ to Level 5 autonomous driving applications. Both companies emphasize that intelligence and AI-driven sensing are crucial for developing safer and high-performing autonomous systems.

title: AdvisorShares Gerber Kawasaki ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the AdvisorShares Gerber Kawasaki ETF (GK), including its current price, category, expenses, holdings, and performance metrics. It also offers insights into its ESG scores, sector allocation, and volatility analysis. The article serves as a comprehensive resource for financial advisors and investors tracking this specific active ETF.

title: Best Buy Is Selling Nvidia RTX 30 Series GPUs At MSRP Tomorrow
summary: Best Buy stores nationwide will be selling Nvidia RTX 30 series graphics cards at their original MSRP starting tomorrow, July 20th. Due to severe shortages and price inflation, this offers a rare opportunity for customers to purchase these GPUs at normal prices. Best Buy will be implementing a ticketing system at participating stores to manage demand and discourage scalping.

title: Nvidia Stock’s Surge Makes Chip Maker 10th-Biggest U.S. Listed Company
summary: Nvidia Corp. has become the 10th-largest U.S. public company due to a surge in its stock, driven by the post-pandemic boom in the semiconductor business. The company's shares have increased by nearly 80% over the past year, resulting in a market value of approximately $453 billion. This valuation exceeds the combined market capitalization of its rivals Intel Corp. and Broadcom Inc.

title: Newcomer Viridi Funds Launches Clean Energy Crypto Mining ETF, 'RIGZ'
summary: Viridi Funds has launched its first ETF, the Viridi Cleaner Energy Crypto-Mining & Semiconductor ETF (RIGZ), offering investors exposure to environmentally sustainable cryptocurrency. The actively managed fund will invest in companies across the crypto mining industry and infrastructure, including semiconductor producers, mining rig manufacturers, and crypto mining companies. RIGZ aims to align purpose and profit by focusing on sustainable practices within the growing crypto ecosystem, particularly in North America where over 50% of Bitcoin mining uses renewable energy sources.

title: Chip design giant Cadence launches AI platform to speed processor development
summary: Cadence Design Systems Inc. has launched Cerebrus Intelligent Chip Explorer, an AI platform designed to accelerate processor development and enhance the productivity of semiconductor engineers. The platform utilizes machine learning, specifically reinforcement learning, to automate and optimize various stages of chip design, including register-transfer level development and floorplan creation. Early adopters like Renesas Electronics Corp. and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd.'s foundry business have already seen significant improvements in chip performance.

title: Intel CEO Says Chip Shortage Could Stretch Into 2023
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger believes the global semiconductor shortage could extend into 2023, joining a growing consensus that supply chain disruptions will persist. The shortage is impacting various industries, leading to rising prices and production delays for goods ranging from consumer gadgets to automobiles. While some easing is expected later this year, a full return to supply-and-demand balance in the semiconductor industry could take one to two years due to the time required to build manufacturing capacity.

title: Cyberpower Hyper Liquid Ultra RTX PC
summary: This article reviews Cyberpower's high-end Hyper Liquid Ultra RTX PC, priced at £4,899. It highlights the system's powerful components, including a watercooled AMD Ryzen 9 5950X and Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti, and critically assesses its build and performance. While praising the component selection generally, the review points out areas for improvement such as the motherboard choice, idle noise levels, and RGB control.

title: FTC changes course on prior approval for reattempted mergers
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has voted to rescind a 1995 policy statement, allowing them to routinely require prior approval for reattempted mergers and prior notice for mergers below the Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) threshold. This move, initiated by FTC Chairman Lina Khan and following President Biden's executive order, aims to bolster protections against unlawful mergers and acquisitions by removing the need for new, time-consuming investigations into deals previously deemed anticompetitive. While supported by a 3-2 vote, Commissioner Noah Phillips expressed concerns that ignoring market changes could hinder normal market operations.

title: As global demand for microchips surges, tech giants go all-in on Israel
summary: Amid a global surge in microchip demand and a component shortage, major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Intel, and Nvidia are establishing or expanding chip design operations in Israel. The country is benefiting from its strong R&D capabilities and skilled workforce in semiconductor design. This trend is attracting increased venture capital investment, despite challenges like a shortage of engineers and rising salaries.

title: Upcoming DL RecSys Summit: Develop and Optimize Deep Learning Recommender Systems
summary: NVIDIA, Facebook, and TensorFlow are hosting a summit on July 29 to discuss best practices for developing and optimizing deep learning recommender systems. The event will feature sessions covering high-performance model training, architectural optimization, and using TensorFlow Recommenders. Experts from these companies will share insights to help engineers and data scientists build effective recommender systems.

title: Intel to build Qualcomm chips, aims to catch foundry rivals by 2025
summary: Intel announced its factories will begin building chips for Qualcomm and Amazon, aiming to regain its leadership in chip manufacturing by 2025 against rivals like TSMC and Samsung. The company outlined a new roadmap with five chipmaking technologies and a revised naming scheme to reflect its competitive standing. This move signifies Intel's commitment to overcoming past delays and establishing itself as a leading foundry.

title: ANNUAL REPORT 2021 Arm: Business Strategy
summary: Arm's 2021 annual report highlights its business strategy as a leader in semiconductor technology, emphasizing its licensing model and significant investments in R&D since being acquired by SoftBank Group in 2016. The report details how these investments are leading to increasing revenue growth, particularly from 5G smartphone sales and the emerging Arm-based server chip market, despite challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic. It also touches on future growth drivers, including new markets like IoT and autonomous vehicles, and the planned sale of Arm to NVIDIA.

title: Corsair One a200 gaming PC review
summary: The Corsair One a200 is a compact gaming PC that combines an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X CPU and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 GPU in a small form factor, delivering excellent 4K gaming performance. Despite its size, it manages impressive thermal performance for the GPU due to a dual-liquid cooling system, although the CPU runs a bit hot. The PC is praised for its powerful components, ease of setup, and quiet operation, though its upgradeability is limited compared to larger systems.

title: OpenAI debuts new AI programming language for creating neural networks
summary: OpenAI has released Triton 1.0, a new programming language designed to simplify and accelerate the creation of high-speed machine learning algorithms, especially those running on Nvidia GPUs. Triton automates complex code optimizations previously requiring extensive CUDA experience, thereby speeding up AI projects and enabling more efficient algorithm development. It optimizes data movement between GPU memory, data distribution across SRAM circuits, and calculation distribution across CUDA cores.

title: AI on the bench: Cadence offers machine learning to smooth chip design
summary: Cadence Design Systems has released Cerebrus Intelligent Chip Explorer, a new software program that uses machine learning to automate aspects of chip design. This tool aims to enhance human productivity by an order of magnitude and improve chip quality metrics like power, performance, and area (PPA) by up to 20%. Cerebrus leverages reinforcement learning to run numerous experiments simultaneously, assisting designers in finding optimal solutions for increasingly complex chip architectures.

title: NVIDIA Advances Instant AI with North American Availability of Base Command Platform
summary: NVIDIA has announced the North American availability of its Base Command Platform, a hosted AI development hub providing instant access to NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD supercomputers. This platform, hosted by Equinix and part of the NVIDIA AI LaunchPad program, is designed for enterprises with large-scale, multi-user AI workflows, enabling them to accelerate AI projects from prototype to production. Adobe is an early adopter, exploring its potential to streamline machine learning development, and the platform is supported by partners like NetApp and Weights & Biases for integrated data management and MLOps tools.

title: U.K. Considers Blocking Nvidia Takeover of Arm Over Security
summary: The U.K. government is reportedly considering blocking Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to potential national security concerns. This move could complicate Nvidia's push to expand its presence in the semiconductor market through the deal with Japan's SoftBank Group Corp.

title: The U.K. may block Nvidia’s acquisition of Arm over security risks
summary: The U.K. government is considering blocking Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to potential national security concerns. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) delivered an assessment with worrying implications, leading the U.K. to be inclined to reject the takeover or impose strict conditions. Arm's critical role in the semiconductor industry and Nvidia's status as a direct competitor to many of Arm's customers are central to the concerns, prompting Nvidia to state its commitment to addressing any issues the U.K. government may have.

title: Zero Waste with Taste: Startup Uses AI to Drive Sustainable Fashion
summary: Heartdub, an AI startup and NVIDIA Inception member, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by using AI to create virtual garments and reduce waste. Their software digitizes textiles and simulates how clothes appear on the human body, significantly cutting down on physical samples, R&D costs, and lead times. This technology aims to help companies achieve zero-waste manufacturing and allows consumers to visualize clothing on digital avatars based on their own measurements.

title: Microchip Technology sees record sales as computer chip supply issues persist
summary: Microchip Technology (MCHP) reported record-setting sales at the beginning of its 2022 fiscal year, driven by the ongoing global demand for computer chips. CEO Ganesh Moorthy indicated that the entire semiconductor supply chain remains constrained, suggesting that chip shortages will extend into 2022. The company, based in Chandler, is experiencing strong demand amidst an industry-wide supply crunch.

title: NVIDIA maintains dominant position in 2020 market for AI processors for cloud and data center
summary: NVIDIA maintained its dominant position in the 2020 global market for AI processors used in cloud and data centers, holding an 80.6% share of global revenue. The company generated $3.2 billion in cloud and data center AI processor revenue, up from $1.8 billion in 2019, primarily due to its leadership in GPU-derived chips. Omdia predicts that alternative suppliers will gain significant market share in the coming years despite NVIDIA's current advantage.

title: Colorful Releases Special Edition iGame RTX 3070 LHR For Bilibili E-Sports Team
summary: Colorful has released a special edition iGame RTX 3070 LHR graphics card exclusively for China's Bilibili E-Sports team and market. This unique card features a 12-pin power connection and a dual-fan design similar to RTX 3080 and RTX 3090 Founders Edition cards. It offers a slight overclocking boost and a low hash rate, tailored for the e-sports segment in specified regions.

title: Qualcomm Bids Against Magna For Veoneer
summary: Qualcomm has made a $4.6 billion offer to acquire Swedish automotive technology supplier Veoneer, outbidding Magna International's previous $3.8 billion proposal. This move aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand its presence in the automotive market, particularly in ADAS and autonomous control systems, leveraging their existing collaboration with Veoneer. The acquisition would allow Qualcomm to offer a complete hardware and software stack to various automotive players, enhancing its growing automotive revenue stream.

title: Cattle-ist for the Future: Plainsight Revolutionizes Livestock Management with AI
summary: Plainsight, an NVIDIA Metropolis partner, is leveraging vision AI and NVIDIA GPUs to revolutionize livestock management. Their system improves accuracy in cattle counting and health monitoring, reducing financial losses and enhancing overall operational efficiency for companies like JBS USA. Beyond managing livestock, Plainsight is also collaborating with CattlePass to use vision AI for tracking cattle on the blockchain, creating digital assets with verifiable ownership and transparent lifecycle records.

title: All AI Do Is Win: NVIDIA Research Nabs ‘Best in Show’ With Digital Avatars at SIGGRAPH
summary: NVIDIA Research received the ‘Best in Show’ award at SIGGRAPH 2021 for their digital avatar technology, which integrates four AI models. This technology allows for the creation of lifelike virtual characters from a single photo, natural 3D facial animation, and text-to-speech conversion. This collaboration leverages NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a cloud-native software suite optimized for VMware vSphere on NVIDIA-Certified Systems, and NetApp's enterprise-class storage. The integrated solution facilitates rapid deployment, management, and scaling of AI workloads in hybrid cloud environments, exemplified by NetApp's GPU-enabled Lab on Demand.

summary: NVIDIA announced the acquisition of Oski Technology, a company specializing in formal verification methods. This acquisition aims to significantly increase NVIDIA's investment and commitment to formal verification strategies, which are crucial for ensuring the correctness of complex modern processors and new autonomous machine applications. Oski, known for its leading-edge work and expertise, has been a long-time partner of NVIDIA, and most of its employees will join NVIDIA, expanding NVIDIA's engineering presence in India.

summary: China is making significant strides in the development and deployment of robotaxis, with several leading companies actively testing and expanding their services. These companies, including AutoX, Baidu Apollo, Momenta, Pony.ai, and WeRide, are moving from trials with safety drivers to driverless operations, integrating advanced technologies like 5G-based C-V2X systems. The long-term strategy involves expanding robotaxi services and applying their underlying technology to other mobility solutions like autonomous buses and last-mile delivery.

summary: The EU is expected to launch an extended antitrust investigation into Nvidia's $54 billion bid for British chip designer ARM. This comes after remedies offered by Nvidia last week failed to address competition concerns, marking a second setback for the company after a similar warning from Britain's antitrust agency. The European Commission is scheduled to end its preliminary review on October 27, initiating a four-month investigation.

summary: Aruba has partnered with Pensando to unveil the CX 10000, a 48-port L2/L3 Ethernet switch featuring embedded Pensando ASICs for security services, load balancing, and firewalls. This distributed data center switch allows companies to build a switching fabric across multiple locations and integrates security directly at the leaf level to enhance performance. While it pushes for a change in traditional separate management of switching and security, analysts predict a significant future market for such integrated distributed switches, especially for large enterprises.

summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation cloud gaming platform, GeForce NOW, which will offer GeForce RTX 3080-class gaming performance through a new high-performance membership tier. summary: Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) reported significant revenue growth for its third fiscal quarter of 2021, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of revenue increase, driven primarily by its Enterprise, Embedded and Semi-custom segment. The company recorded $4.3 billion in net sales, representing a 54% annual and 12% sequential growth, with strong contributions from data center and custom-design chips. summary: Intel Corp and Google Cloud have collaborated to create "Mount Evans," a new class of chip called an "infrastructure processing unit" (IPU) aimed at optimizing cloud computing data centers. The government seeks to attract investors by providing financial support and tax reductions, anticipating a surge in semiconductor demand as India's electronics production rapidly grows.
