summary: Arista Networks experienced significant stock gains following strong earnings and boosted guidance, driven by increased capital spending from hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft. The company also continues to gain market share from competitors like Cisco in both data center, cloud, and campus networking segments, indicating a robust cloud boom across the industry. Other infrastructure vendors like NVIDIA, Amazon Web Services, and Broadcom are also seeing growth.

title: GOI to launch a mega-billion plan for semiconductor manufacturers
summary: The Indian government is set to introduce a significant capital and production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme to boost domestic semiconductor manufacturing, addressing global chip shortages. This initiative involves discussions with major global chipmakers like TSMC and Intel, offering financial support, tariff cuts, and leveraging programs like SPECS. The move aims to capitalize on rising domestic demand, project electronic production to reach $350-400 billion by 2025, and attract investments following China's "Plus One" policy.

title: How Intel plans to catch Samsung and TSMC and regain its dominance in the chip market
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has outlined an ambitious plan to regain dominance in the chip market by 2025, aiming to surpass competitors Samsung and TSMC. The strategy involves significant investment in new fabrication plants globally, totaling over $44 billion, and opening Intel's fabs to other companies through Intel Foundry Services. This move addresses past production missteps and aims to leverage government subsidies like the CHIPS Act to boost U.S. chip manufacturing.

title: EXPLAINED: What is Metaverse and Why Facebook/ Meta Thinks it's the Future of Internet
summary: This article explains the concept of the metaverse, why Facebook (now Meta) views it as the future of the internet, and what its potential applications are. It details how the metaverse would work, from virtual interactions and business opportunities to the technologies being developed to build it, while also touching on data privacy concerns.

title: AMD Blitzes Intel, Nvidia With New Faster EPYC, Instinct Chips
summary: AMD announced new EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs aimed at challenging Intel and Nvidia in data center workloads for high-performance computing and AI. The new EPYC processors (Milan-X) feature 3D chiplet technology to triple L3 cache, dramatically increasing performance, especially for technical computing. The Instinct MI200 series GPUs are positioned as "the world's fastest HPC and AI accelerator," promising up to 4.9 times faster HPC and 20 percent faster AI performance compared to Nvidia’s A100 GPU.

title: AMD lands Meta as customer and takes on Nvidia, sending shares up 11%
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares rose 11% after announcing Meta Platforms Inc. as a new data center chip customer, intensifying its competition with Intel. AMD also unveiled new chips, including the MI200 for AI and machine learning to challenge Nvidia, and the Bergamo processor for cloud computing to compete with Ampere Computing. These strategic moves bolster AMD's market position against larger rivals and secure its presence with major cloud providers.

title: Innoviz Perception Solution Supported on NVIDIA DRIVE Platform
summary: Innoviz Technologies announced that its advanced perception solution is now supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE platform, integrating its LiDAR sensor and perception software into NVIDIA's end-to-end AI platform for autonomous vehicles. This collaboration allows Innoviz's technology to enable object detection, tracking, and classification, as well as obstacle detection and calibration, and is integrated with NVIDIA DRIVE Sim for development and validation. The partnership aims to accelerate the development and deployment of autonomous vehicles by providing customer access to Innoviz's LiDAR solutions within the NVIDIA DRIVE ecosystem.

title: Supermicro Enhances Broadest Portfolio of Edge to Cloud AI Systems with Accelerated Inferencing and New Intelligent Fabric Support
summary: Supermicro announced enhancements to its AI GPU server portfolio, integrating new NVIDIA Ampere-family GPUs to deliver up to 10x faster AI inference performance and 3x faster training. These systems are designed for a wide range of applications from edge computing to cloud environments, critical for uses like autonomous driving, video streaming, and cloud gaming. Supermicro also introduced its Universal GPU Platform and systems supporting the new NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand product line, alongside optimized solutions for NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise.

title: Nvidia picks Luminar's lidar for self-driving tech, sending its shares up 15%
summary: Luminar Technologies Inc. saw its stock jump 15% after Nvidia announced it would use Luminar's lidar technology for its self-driving platforms. This news coincided with Nvidia's annual GTC conference. Luminar has also recently partnered with Volvo and is expanding into the Chinese market.

title: NVIDIA Announces Omniverse Replicator Synthetic-Data-Generation Engine for Training AIs
summary: NVIDIA has announced Omniverse Replicator, a powerful synthetic-data-generation engine designed to produce physically simulated synthetic data for training deep neural networks. The first applications, NVIDIA DRIVE Sim and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, will accelerate the development of autonomous vehicles and robots by generating diverse and accurate datasets that cover rare or dangerous scenarios. This technology aims to augment real-world data, enabling developers to create high-quality AI models and generate ground truth data that is challenging for humans to label.

title: A First-Class Experience, for Every Car: Meet NVIDIA DRIVE Concierge and Chauffeur, Built With Omniverse Avatar
summary: NVIDIA has introduced DRIVE Concierge and DRIVE Chauffeur, AI platforms designed to enhance safety, convenience, and intelligence in personal vehicles. DRIVE Concierge acts as an intelligent in-car assistant using NVIDIA Omniverse Avatar for real-time conversational AI, while DRIVE Chauffeur is an AI-assisted driving platform capable of handling urban and highway traffic autonomously. Both systems work in conjunction to transform the driving experience, making it safer and more enjoyable.

title: NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Combines Orin With Best-in-Class Sensor Architecture for Production-Ready Platform
summary: NVIDIA has announced its DRIVE Hyperion 8 platform, a production-ready computer architecture and sensor set for full self-driving systems, available for 2024 vehicle models. The platform leverages two NVIDIA DRIVE Orin systems-on-a-chip for redundancy and ample compute, supported by a comprehensive sensor suite from leading suppliers like Continental, Hella, Luminar, Sony, and Valeo. Designed to be open and modular, DRIVE Hyperion 8 aims to accelerate the development and deployment of safe and robust autonomous vehicles.

title: NVIDIA Announces Platform for Creating AI Avatars
summary: NVIDIA has introduced Omniverse Avatar, a new AI platform designed for creating interactive AI avatars capable of engaging in real-time conversations. This platform integrates several NVIDIA technologies, including speech AI, computer vision, natural language understanding, and simulation, enabling avatars to see, speak, and comprehend human intent. Omniverse Avatar is intended to revolutionize customer service interactions across various industries by providing customizable AI assistants.

title: NVIDIA Opens New Portals Into Virtual Worlds With Expanded Omniverse Ecosystem and Capabilities
summary: NVIDIA has expanded its Omniverse ecosystem with new features and partnerships, enhancing its physically accurate 3D virtual world platform. The updates include AR, VR, multi-GPU rendering, and new technologies like Omniverse Avatar and Replicator, alongside integrations with Bentley Systems and Esri for industrial digital-twin applications. Omniverse Enterprise has also reached general availability, enabling real-time collaboration for global 3D design teams across various industries.

title: NVIDIA Brings AI to the Supply Chain
summary: NVIDIA has introduced NVIDIA cuOpt AI software to help optimize the $9 trillion logistics industry amidst global supply chain disruptions. This software uses AI to improve route planning, warehouse operations, and fleet management, aiming to reduce delivery costs and enhance efficiency. Domino's Pizza has already seen promising results using cuOpt for real-time delivery optimization.

title: NVIDIA Brings Large Language AI Models to Enterprises Worldwide
summary: NVIDIA has introduced new tools to enable enterprises worldwide to develop and deploy large language models (LLMs) for domain-specific AI applications. This includes the NVIDIA NeMo Megatron framework for training LLMs with trillions of parameters, the customizable Megatron 530B LLM, and the NVIDIA Triton Inference Server with multi-GPU, multinode functionality. These technologies aim to simplify the creation and deployment of advanced language-based AI, making it accessible for various industries and scientific research.

title: Luminar Lidar Selected for NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Autonomous Vehicle Reference Platform
summary: Luminar's lidar solution has been selected to be part of the sensor suite in the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion autonomous vehicle reference platform, which aims to accelerate the development of autonomous consumer vehicles with production starting in 2024. The platform will utilize Luminar's long-range Iris lidar for Level 3 highway driving, integrating it with NVIDIA’s high-performance compute and AI software. This collaboration is expected to provide automakers with an advanced platform for next-generation safety and autonomous capabilities.

title: CoreWeave, Specialized Cloud Provider, Raises $50 Million in New Capital from Magnetar
summary: CoreWeave, a specialized cloud provider focused on NVIDIA GPU-accelerated workloads, announced it has raised $50 million from Magnetar Capital to expand its infrastructure. This funding follows a period of significant growth for CoreWeave, with its total revenues on track to triple in 2021 and its cloud business experiencing 271% growth in the last three months. The investment will enable CoreWeave to further scale its offerings for high-performance computing, catering to diverse needs such as VFX rendering, machine learning, and digital assets.

title: AMD wins Meta as a data centre customer
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) has secured Meta (formerly Facebook) as a data centre chip customer, leading to an 11% surge in AMD's shares. This win highlights AMD's growing market presence against competitors like Nvidia and Intel, especially with the launch of new chips like the MI200 for AI and machine learning, and "Bergamo" for cloud computing. The deal adds Meta to AMD's list of major clients, which already includes Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft Azure.

title: Nvidia CEO: ‘We don’t have any magic bullets’ to deal with chip shortage
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that the global chip shortage is not expected to end soon, with demand continuing to outstrip supply through the next year. He noted that while Nvidia is fortunate to have diverse suppliers, there are no "magic bullets" to navigate the supply chain issues. Huang believes that the increased demand for chips, driven by factors like remote work and gaming, represents a permanent shift rather than a temporary trend.

title: Aeva and Luminar deals show lidar gaining traction
summary: Aeva and Luminar, two lidar companies that recently went public via SPACs, are gaining traction in the autonomous vehicle industry. Aeva has partnered with Fabrinet for mass production of its chip-scale lidar modules, while Luminar's lidar has been selected for Nvidia's DRIVE Hyperion platform. Another lidar startup, Ouster, also reported a significant increase in sales and plans to launch a new automotive lidar platform.

title: TSMC and Sony partner to build US$7bn chip factory in Japan
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Sony have announced a joint venture to build a $7 billion chip plant in Japan, aiming for mass production by 2024. The new factory in Kumamoto will be TSMC's first in Japan, creating 1,500 high-tech jobs and producing 45,000 12-inch wafers per month to address the global semiconductor shortage. Sony will invest $500 million for a 20% equity stake, with significant funding also provided by the Japanese government.

title: Samsung Announces Availability of Its Leading-Edge 2.5D Integration ‘H-Cube’ Solution for High Performance Applications
summary: Samsung Electronics has announced the availability of its new Hybrid-Substrate Cube (H-Cube) technology, a 2.5D packaging solution for high-performance computing (HPC), AI, data center, and network products. Developed in collaboration with Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Amkor Technology, H-Cube uses an advanced silicon interposer and hybrid-substrate structure to efficiently integrate up to six HBMs, providing a cost-effective solution for large-area packaging challenges. This innovation seeks to address increasing integration requirements and substrate supply constraints in the semiconductor industry.

title: NVIDIA highlights healthcare AI innovations
summary: NVIDIA announced new AI technologies and tools designed to transform healthcare, including the Clara Holoscan platform for software-defined medical devices. The company's CEO, Jensen Huang, emphasized how AI and physics machine learning will revolutionize medical instruments and drug discovery. The article details how Clara Holoscan accelerates data processing in medical devices and highlights Clara Discovery's role in speeding up drug discovery by overcoming molecular simulation bottlenecks.

title: Sony slashes PlayStation 5 production target amid chip shortage, supply chain challenges: report
summary: Sony has reportedly lowered its PlayStation 5 production target for the current fiscal year due to global chip shortages and supply chain disruptions. The company now expects to produce about 15 million PS5s, down from an earlier target of over 16 million, impacting availability during the holiday season. Sony is investing in a new chip factory in Japan with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) to ease future supply constraints, while rival Nintendo has also revised its sales forecast downwards due to similar issues.

title: COLORFUL Unveils GeForce RTX 3070 Customization Series Graphics Cards
summary: COLORFUL has launched its new GeForce RTX 3070 Customization Series graphics cards, designed to replace its Bilibili Edition. The series includes the RTX 3070 and RTX 3070 Ti custom OC variants, featuring a two-sided cooling structure and magnetic interchangeable backplate covers for personalization. These cards are currently listed on COLORFUL's website but are expected to be available only in Chinese markets.

title: Nvidia CEO Huang: We could make ARM successful in ‘all other areas of computing’
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes that even if the acquisition of ARM doesn't go through, Nvidia will continue to thrive by supporting a diverse range of CPUs, seeing opportunities for accelerated computing wherever CPUs are present. Huang also highlighted that integrating ARM with Nvidia could significantly boost ARM's research and development efforts, helping it succeed in various computing sectors beyond its current dominance in mobile devices. The deal faces significant regulatory hurdles in multiple countries, and its outcome will determine the future of the proposed merger.

title: Nvidia CEO: The metaverse will be 'much, much bigger than the physical world'
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes the metaverse will far surpass the physical world in scale and economic activity. He envisions an internet where virtual creations and training for AI and robotics will be significantly larger than real-world counterparts. Nvidia's Omniverse platform is central to this vision, enabling businesses to create digital twins for various applications, including 5G network layout and autonomous driving simulation.

summary: Unity has introduced two new products, Unity Simulation Pro and Unity SystemGraph, designed to simulate AI and robotics deployments for virtual testing and analysis. summary: Qualcomm announced that it will supply chips for BMW's next generation of driver-assistance and self-driving systems, marking a significant diversification beyond its core mobile phone chip business. This move underscores Qualcomm's strategic expansion into the automotive sector, aiming to challenge competitors like Nvidia and Intel in the self-driving technology market. The new chips will be used in BMW's "Neue Klasse" series of cars, with production slated to begin in 2025.

title: Chipmaker Nvidia forecasts robust revenue on AI, metaverse buzz
summary: Nvidia Corp forecasted fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations, driven by growth in its data center business and investments in artificial intelligence and the metaverse. The company's shares rose significantly following the news, reflecting strong demand for its graphics and AI chips in gaming, data centers, and autonomous vehicles. Nvidia's Q3 revenue also surpassed estimates, with significant rises in its gaming and data center units.

title: Texas Instruments to begin construction next year on new 300-mm semiconductor wafer fabrication plants
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) announced plans to begin construction in 2022 on new 300-millimeter semiconductor wafer fabrication plants ("fabs") in Sherman, Texas. This North Texas site could accommodate up to four fabs, with the first two starting construction next year. The investment, potentially reaching $30 billion, aims to meet future demand in industrial and automotive markets and strengthen TI's manufacturing capabilities.

title: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) Q3 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: NVIDIA reported an outstanding Q3 2021 with record revenue of $7.1 billion, up 50% year-on-year, driven by strong performance in Gaming, Data Center, and Professional Visualization. The company highlighted the expansion of its RTX technology in gaming and creative applications, the growing adoption of Omniverse for digital twins and AI avatars, and significant advancements in its Data Center business with AI inference and enterprise solutions. NVIDIA also addressed the status of its proposed acquisition of Arm and provided a positive outlook for future growth, particularly in the Data Center segment.

title: Enphase Energy CEO Says You Should 'Stop Doing Stupid Things'
summary: Enphase Energy CEO Badrinarayanan Kothandaraman, 48, has led a significant financial turnaround for the solar products maker by applying principles of thrift and simplicity learned from his upbringing in India. His strategy focused on cutting costs, boosting gross margins, and fostering strong supplier and customer relationships, including a shift to competitively bidding for components and moving engineering staff to India. Under his leadership, Enphase joined the S&P 500, with revenue and share prices seeing substantial growth, driven by its microinverter technology and expansion into energy storage.

title: Ford, GlobalFoundries say they will work together to boost chip supply
summary: Ford Motor Co. and chip manufacturer GlobalFoundries Inc. announced a non-binding agreement to boost chip supplies for Ford's vehicles and the U.S. auto industry. The collaboration will explore increasing production capacity for Ford's current lineup and conduct joint research and development on crucial chips for future cars, such as battery-management systems and self-driving technologies. This initiative aims to address the global chip shortage that has impacted vehicle production and represents Ford's strategy to vertically integrate key technologies.

title: NVDA Earnings: Nvidia Q3 profit, revenue beat Street view amid strong chip demand
summary: Nvidia Corporation reported a significant 50% increase in third-quarter revenues, surpassing Wall Street expectations for both earnings and revenue. This growth was driven by strong demand for data-center and gaming chips, with adjusted earnings reaching $1.17 per share and net income climbing to $2.46 billion. Record revenues from gaming, data center, and professional visualization platforms contributed to the strong financial performance.

title: NVIDIA CEO Receives Semiconductor Industry’s Top Honor
summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, was awarded the Semiconductor Industry Association's (SIA) highest honor, the Robert N. Noyce award, for his pioneering work in accelerated computing. The award ceremony highlighted NVIDIA's significant impact on the industry and AI development. Huang shared his journey from early programming to founding NVIDIA and his vision for advanced computing applications like Earth-2 for climate science.

title: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon Elected Chair of Semiconductor Industry Association
summary: Cristiano Amon, President and CEO of Qualcomm Incorporated, has been elected as the 2022 chair of the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA). Matt Johnson, President of Silicon Labs, was elected SIA vice chair. Amon's extensive background in engineering and leadership roles at Qualcomm, including shaping its 5G strategy and business diversification, positions him to lead the SIA in advocating for policies that promote industry growth, innovation, national security, and global technology leadership.

title: Global X signals intent in Europe with seven thematic ETF launches
summary: Global X has launched seven new thematic ETFs in Europe, expanding its UCITS range to 12 products. These ETFs cover various themes including autonomous vehicles, clean tech, cybersecurity, e-commerce, fintech, IoT, and robotics/AI, with TERs ranging from 0.50% to 0.60%. This move signifies Global X's robust growth and commitment to offering targeted exposure to disruptive global themes for European investors.

title: Nvidia jumps after big data centre growth boosts outlook
summary: Nvidia's stock jumped after the company reported strong revenue forecasts, driven by significant growth in its data center segment. While gaming chip sales remain strong, and the company sees potential in the metaverse and cryptocurrency mining, its proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. faces regulatory challenges. Nvidia's market capitalization has soared, placing it among the top S&P 500 companies.

title: Habana Labs AI Training Solution Featuring Supermicro X12 Gaudi AI Training Server With DDN AI400X2 Storage System
summary: Habana Labs, an Intel company, has announced a new enterprise AI training solution that combines the Supermicro X12 Gaudi AI training server with the DDN AI400X2 storage system. This collaboration aims to provide a cost-efficient, scalable, and easy-to-use solution that eliminates storage bottlenecks and optimizes AI compute capacity utilization. The integrated system is designed to address the increasing demand for AI training and model rebuilding while keeping costs down for enterprise customers.

title: NVIDIA BlueField DPU Ecosystem Expands as Partners Introduce Joint Solutions
summary: NVIDIA has expanded its BlueField DPU ecosystem by introducing the DOCA 1.2 software framework, enabling partners to develop zero-trust solutions. Industry leaders like Red Hat, Juniper Networks, F5, Excelero, and DDN are integrating their technologies with BlueField DPUs and the DOCA architecture to enhance cybersecurity and storage performance. The DOCA software framework is currently available for early access, providing developers with the tools to accelerate software-defined management services.

title: Federated Learning With FLARE: NVIDIA Brings Collaborative AI to Healthcare and Beyond
summary: NVIDIA has open-sourced NVIDIA FLARE, a software development kit designed to facilitate federated learning, particularly in data-sensitive fields like healthcare. This technology enables collaborative AI model training without centralizing proprietary datasets, addressing issues of data scarcity, privacy, and bias. FLARE supports various federated learning architectures and is already being integrated into healthcare AI platforms and projects to accelerate research and development across multiple industries.

title: AutoSens Awards AEye Founder and Chief Technology Officer Luis Dussan the 2020 Vision Award
summary: AEye founder and CTO Luis Dussan has been honored with the 2020 Vision Award by AutoSens for his significant contributions to the vehicle perception ecosystem. Dussan's background in military targeting systems informed his development of AEye's adaptive LiDAR, which uses AI and edge processing to enhance perception for autonomous vehicles. This technology focuses on moving complexity to software to deliver higher quality information with less data, improving situational awareness and detection probability.

title: META ETF: 10 Things to Know About the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF
summary: The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) is gaining investor attention due to increased interest in Metaverse-focused ETFs, especially with new launches in the space. Launched on June 30, 2021, METV invests in companies related to the Metaverse, such as computing, networking, and virtual platform firms, aiming to track the performance of the Ball Metaverse Index. The ETF currently holds 40 companies, including potential exposure to Nvidia, Roblox, and Tencent, and has an expense ratio of 0.75%.

title: Amazon's cloud unit launches new chips to take on Intel, Nvidia
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has introduced two new custom computing chips, Graviton3 and Trainium, aimed at competing with offerings from Intel, AMD, and Nvidia. AWS claims its new chips offer better performance per dollar and lower costs for machine learning model training compared to its rivals. This move signals AWS's continued drive to develop its own hardware and intensify competition in the cloud computing and chip markets.

title: How a Stanford couple created Taiwan’s best-known AI start-up
summary: This article details how a Stanford couple, Chih-Han Yu and Winnie Lee, founded Appier, Taiwan's first AI unicorn. After eight failed attempts and nearly two decades, their company, which develops AI-based precision marketing solutions, went public on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in March, becoming a success story for both Taiwan's tech scene and Japan's IPO market.

title: U.S. Sues to Block Nvidia’s $40 Billion Chip Takeover of Arm
summary: U.S. antitrust officials have sued to block Nvidia's proposed $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd., arguing the deal would stifle innovation in the semiconductor industry. The Federal Trade Commission stated that the takeover would give Nvidia undue control over chip designs used across various technology sectors, impacting its rivals and potentially leading to higher prices. This challenge comes amidst a global chip shortage.

title: FTC Sues To Block $40 Billion Nvidia - Arm Computer Chip Deal
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has sued to block Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of chip designer Arm Ltd., citing concerns that the deal would stifle competition and innovation in the semiconductor industry. Regulators in the U.K. and EU are also investigating the proposed merger. Nvidia, based in Santa Clara, California, vowed to contest the lawsuit and preserve Arm's open licensing model.

title: FTC Challenges Nvidia’s Deal for Arm Holdings
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has filed a lawsuit to block Nvidia Corp.'s proposed acquisition of Arm Holdings. The FTC argues that the semiconductor deal is anticompetitive, signaling a potentially aggressive antitrust enforcement effort under Chairwoman Lina Khan. This legal challenge initiates a significant antitrust campaign by the agency.

title: U.S. sues to block Nvidia’s $40-billion chip takeover of Arm
summary: U.S. antitrust officials have sued to block Nvidia's proposed $40-billion acquisition of Arm Ltd., citing concerns that the deal would stifle innovation and undermine competition in the semiconductor industry. The Federal Trade Commission argues that the merger would grant Nvidia excessive control over chip designs widely used across various technologies. The acquisition, initially valued at $40 billion in September 2020, has faced regulatory hurdles globally due to Arm's critical role as a technology licensor to hundreds of companies including Nvidia's rivals.

title: US sues to block Nvidia deal to buy British chipmaker Arm
summary: The United States Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has sued to block Nvidia's planned $75bn acquisition of British chip design provider Arm, citing concerns that the deal would give Nvidia control over crucial computing technology and design relied upon by competitors. The FTC argues that the merger could undermine competition, leading to reduced product quality, less innovation, higher prices, and limited choices for consumers. Despite the legal challenge and opposition from other regulators, Nvidia shares remained largely unchanged due to investor focus on its growing data center business.

title: Regulators in US, UK, EU All Alarmed By Chip Maker Nvidia’s $40B Deal to Buy Chip Designer
summary: Regulators in the U.S., U.K., and E.U. are expressing alarm over Nvidia Corporation's $40 billion proposed acquisition of chip designer Arm Ltd. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has filed a lawsuit to block the deal, citing concerns that it would grant Nvidia too much power and stifle competition and innovation in the semiconductor industry. Nvidia, however, maintains that the merger would benefit the industry, promote competition, and preserve Arm's open licensing model.

title: Nvidia's $40 billion Arm acquisition is now ‘highly unlikely’ to go through, analyst says
summary: Gartner semiconductor analyst Alan Priestley believes Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of U.K. chip designer Arm is "highly unlikely" to be completed due to increasing regulatory probes in multiple regions. The deal, initially expected by March 2022, faces antitrust concerns from regulators and industry rivals who fear it could restrict access to Arm's neutral chip designs. If the acquisition fails, SoftBank, Arm's current owner, is expected to pursue an initial public offering (IPO) for the company.

title: U.S. FTC sues to block Nvidia deal to buy Arm
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has sued to block Nvidia Corp's more than $80 billion acquisition of British chip technology provider Arm, citing concerns that the deal would give Nvidia undue control over crucial computing technology and designs. This move complicates an already challenging regulatory path for the acquisition, which has faced opposition from the chip industry and scrutiny from British and European Union regulators. The FTC argues the merger would harm competition, reduce innovation, and lead to higher prices by giving Nvidia the ability and incentive to undermine competitors who rely on Arm's technology.

title: US challenges Nvidia takeover of chip designer Arm
summary: The US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has challenged Nvidia's proposed acquisition of chip designer Arm, arguing it would give Nvidia too much control over crucial computing technology and harm competition. Nvidia had planned to complete the deal by March 2022 and stated it would work to prove the transaction's benefits to the industry. The acquisition has already faced scrutiny and legal challenges from regulators in the UK and Europe.

title: Is Texas America’s Rising Semiconductor Hotspot?
summary: Texas is rapidly becoming a major hub for semiconductor development, attracting large corporations like Samsung and Tesla due to its business-friendly climate, lack of corporate and personal income taxes, and abundant skilled workforce. The state boasts a robust academic system and ample space for development, making it an ideal location for the expansion of semiconductor manufacturing. With significant investments from companies like Texas Instruments and Samsung, coupled with state and potential federal incentives, Texas aims to solidify its position as a self-sufficient leader in the semiconductor industry and create thousands of new jobs.

title: Nasdaq dives over 2% as tech stocks slide at end of volatile week
summary: Wall Street's major indexes, particularly the Nasdaq, experienced a significant decline as tech stocks slid at the end of a volatile week. This downturn was influenced by mixed jobs data, uncertainty surrounding the Omicron coronavirus variant, and the Federal Reserve's policy tightening signals. Major tech companies such as Apple, Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla all saw their shares fall, contributing to the broader market dip.

title: Nvidia metaverse future bright even as Arm may slip from grasp
summary: Nvidia's acquisition of British chip technology provider Arm faces significant hurdles, with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission suing to block the deal and analysts doubting its completion. Despite this potential setback, Nvidia's future prospects remain strong, driven by its focus on artificial intelligence (AI) and the metaverse, areas where it is a leading player. The company's data center business is thriving as internet companies invest heavily in augmented and virtual reality technologies.

title: EU regulators pause investigation into Nvidia, ARM deal
summary: EU antitrust regulators have temporarily halted their investigation into Nvidia's bid for British chip designer ARM, awaiting more information. This pause follows the U.S. Federal Trade Commission's lawsuit to block the deal and the EU's previous warning that the acquisition could harm competition. The delay is similar to others seen during the COVID-19 pandemic due to data gathering challenges.

title: U.S. says Nvidia-Arm deal harms market for networking, self-driving car chips
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has argued that Nvidia's $80 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. would harm competition in emerging markets for self-driving car chips and data processing units. The FTC believes that chip companies relying on Arm would hesitate to work closely with it due to fears of Nvidia accessing their product plans. Nvidia maintains the deal will benefit the industry and promote competition against Intel's x86 architecture.

title: Intel plans to take self-driving car unit public in the U.S. in mid-2022
summary: Intel announced its plan to take its self-driving car unit, Mobileye, public in the U.S. in mid-2022 through an IPO. Intel acquired Mobileye for $15.3 billion in 2017, and the IPO is expected to value Mobileye at over $50 billion, creating value for Intel shareholders who will remain majority owners. This move aims to give Mobileye more visibility and help fund Intel's expansion plans, including building new chip plants.

title: Intel plans to take self-driving car unit Mobileye public
summary: Intel announced its plan to take its self-driving car unit, Mobileye, public in the United States by mid-2022. This deal could value Mobileye at over $50 billion, with Intel intending to retain majority ownership and Mobileye's executive team. The move aims to build on Mobileye's innovation track record and unlock value for shareholders, as Intel faces pressure from activist investors regarding its chip manufacturing operations.

title: Accelerating Financial Services With AI
summary: This article highlights how AI is transforming the financial services industry, from traditional banks to fintechs. It showcases various use cases such as preventing fraud, automating insurance claims, and accelerating trading strategies, featuring companies like Capital One, Intuit, Square, Ping An, CAPE Analytics, and Applica. The article emphasizes AI's role in improving customer service, reducing costs, and enhancing efficiency across different financial sectors.

summary: The BlackRock Future U.S. Themes ETF (BTHM) is an actively managed ETF launched on December 14, 2021, focusing on US stocks that provide exposure to emerging and structural themes. Its top holdings include NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: Research at Microsoft 2021: Collaborating for real-world change
summary: This article details Microsoft Research's 2021 initiatives, emphasizing a shift towards addressing global challenges like climate change, healthcare equity, and digital divides through collaborative innovation. It highlights advancements in AI, such as large language models and computer vision, and showcases efforts in fostering hybrid work, enabling accessibility, and promoting societal resilience and sustainability. The report also underscores the importance of trustworthy AI development, privacy preservation, and engaging with the global research community through fellowships and partnerships.

title: Intel to invest $7 billion in new plant in Malaysia, creating 9,000 jobs
summary: Intel Chief Executive Pat Gelsinger announced a $7 billion investment to build a new chip-packaging and testing factory in Malaysia, creating over 4,000 Intel jobs and more than 5,000 construction jobs. This expansion aims to address the global semiconductor shortage, which Gelsinger expects to persist into 2023. The new advanced packaging facility is projected to begin production in 2024.

title: HSBC raises Taiwan outlook over semiconductor industry
summary: HSBC's global private banking and wealth management division has an optimistic outlook for Taiwan, primarily due to the anticipated continued growth of the semiconductor sector driven by global digitalization. While semiconductor earnings per share growth might slow in the coming year due to a high comparison base, demand is expected to remain strong, especially with new applications for the metaverse. However, PGIM Securities Investment Trust Enterprise Co projected single-digit profit growth for local companies next year, with the electronics sector performing well but conventional industries facing rising raw material costs and the shipping sector struggling with persistent port congestion.

title: Desktop computers and All-in-One PCs
summary: HP offers a wide range of desktop computers and All-in-One PCs designed for various uses, including work, entertainment, gaming, and creative tasks. The article highlights new AI PC models like the HP OmniDesk and OmniStudio X, alongside established lines such as HP Pavilion, Envy, OMEN, and VICTUS, detailing their specifications and intended applications. Customers can filter choices by use case, series, operating system, product type, and screen size to find the perfect device.

The article also includes technical analysis, seasonal trends, and frequently asked questions about ETFs and NIO3's specific characteristics.

title: TSMC introduces new chip technology for datacenters
summary: TSMC has introduced a new semiconductor manufacturing technology called N4X, specifically designed for High Performance Computing (HPC) products. This new process, part of the N5 family, offers significant performance boosts and leverages TSMC's 5nm volume production experience. HPC is identified as TSMC's fastest-growing business segment, and the N4X is expected to enter risk production by the first half of 2023.

title: Investor Alert for Week Ended December 17, 2021
summary: This investor alert discusses the emerging metaverse, Web 3.0, and its potential to revolutionize various sectors including social interaction, commerce, and gaming, comparing its disruptive potential to the early internet. It covers investment opportunities in hardware, software, NFTs, and virtual real estate within this digital ecosystem. Additionally, the report provides an overview of performance and opportunities in airline, emerging markets, energy & natural resources, domestic equities, and crypto sectors, alongside a gold market update.

title: Hesai Technology to exhibit at CES 2022, showcasing its complete portfolio of cutting-edge LiDAR solutions
summary: Hesai Technology, a leader in LiDAR technology, announced its participation in CES 2022 to showcase its full range of LiDAR solutions. The exhibition will feature live demonstrations of their sensors for various applications, including autonomous driving and robotics, and will unveil a new automotive-grade, hybrid solid-state LiDAR for ADAS. Hesai's LiDARs are widely adopted globally by leading autonomous driving developers, OEMs, and robotics companies.

title: Federated learning: Intelligence versus privacy—can we have both?
summary: This article discusses federated learning (FL) as a solution for machine learning at scale while addressing data privacy concerns. It highlights FL's benefits in industries like banking and healthcare, enabling shared AI model training without sharing sensitive data. The article also covers design challenges related to privacy in FL and how NetApp's infrastructure solutions can help in data protection and governance.

summary: The global 3D Machine Vision Market was valued at USD 1.45 Billion in 2020 and is projected to reach USD 2.55 Billion by 2028, exhibiting a CAGR of 10.02% from 2021 to 2028. title: Intel Corp. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors
summary: Intel Corp. (INTC) stock dropped 2.02% on Monday, closing at $49.60, during a generally poor trading day for the stock market. This performance placed Intel below its 52-week high and saw it underperform compared to competitors like NVIDIA Corp., Texas Instruments Inc., and Qualcomm Inc. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Nvidia claims record-breaking BlueField-2 DPU performance tests
summary: Nvidia's BlueField-2 DPUs have demonstrated record-breaking performance in benchmark tests, achieving 41.5 million IOPS. These specialized chips offload infrastructure administration tasks from CPUs, significantly improving overall server performance and efficiency. The company's tests show that BlueField-2 DPUs offer over four times faster input/output operations per second than competing chips, enabling better performance for various enterprise workloads.

title: Market Breadth Showcases Equal-Weight Benefits
summary: The article discusses the benefits of equal-weight strategies in investing, particularly highlighted by current market breadth where a few large-cap tech stocks are dominating the S&P 500. It suggests that while cap-weighted indices show strong performance due to these few stocks, equal-weight ETFs like RSP offer better diversification and can outperform when market leadership narrows, as demonstrated by its recent performance against the S&P 500.

title: Here are the top-performing technology stocks of 2021
summary: This article highlights the top-performing technology stocks of 2021, despite a challenging end to the year for the sector. It focuses on companies like Upstart, Synaptics, Asana, Fortinet, and Nvidia, detailing their impressive growth, revenue figures, and contributions to areas like online lending, IoT, collaboration software, cybersecurity, and high-performance computing. The report underscores how specific companies thrived amidst broader market volatility, with several achieving triple-digit gains.

title: Hyperfine (HYPR) Stock Price, News & Analysis
summary: Hyperfine, Inc. (NASDAQ: HYPR) is a medical technology company focused on portable neuroimaging systems, with its flagship Swoop® MRI system designed for bedside use. title: Apple, Meta, Nvidia Take Top Weightings in ProShares’ Metaverse ETF Filing
summary: ProShares, a major ETF issuer, is seeking to launch a metaverse-themed ETF which will track an index comprising public companies involved in metaverse technologies. Notably, Apple, Nvidia, and Meta (formerly Facebook) will hold the top three weighted positions in this new fund. This move follows the increasing investor interest in the metaverse sector, with the global metaverse ETF market reaching $2.2 billion.

title: Intel appoints 10 Israeli executives to senior global positions
summary: Intel Corporation has appointed 10 Israeli executives to senior global positions, including Karin Eibschitz-Segal as a global corporate vice president, making her the second Israeli woman to hold such a role. The appointments highlight Intel's appreciation for its Israeli human capital and come amidst a global semiconductor shortage, underscoring Israel's growing importance in the tech industry. Intel is the largest private employer in Israel, with significant development centers and manufacturing plants.

title: ProShares Plans To Launch ETF Focused On Metaverse
summary: ProShares, known for launching the first Bitcoin ETF in the U.S., has filed with the SEC to create a new metaverse-focused ETF called the ProShares Metaverse Theme ETF. This ETF aims to track the Solactive Metaverse Theme Index, which includes companies involved in metaverse technologies like Apple, Nvidia, and Meta. This development follows similar moves by Canadian companies and reflects the growing trend of global companies entering the metaverse and NFT space.

title: These are the best-performing S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 stocks of 2021
summary: This article highlights the top-performing stocks in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 for 2021, detailing how the stock market's performance surprised many investors.
